design_detail: 2.5% on the very rich with a high threshold
quote_original: Antaranya ialah menilai kepada pembangunan cukai kekayaan agar kita tidak terlalu bergantung kepada pencukaian berasaskan pendapatan dan perbelanjaan rakyat. Cukai kekayaan ini boleh dikenakan kepada golongan yang sangat kaya dengan meletakkan satu nilai ambang yang tinggi dengan peratusan mengikut peratus zakat iaitu 2.5 peratus.
quote_en: Among them is evaluating the development of a wealth tax so that we do not rely too heavily on taxation based on people's income and expenditure. This wealth tax can be imposed on the very rich by setting a high threshold with a percentage following the zakat rate of 2.5 percent.
source_title: Penyata Rasmi Parlimen Dewan Rakyat DR 16.10.2025
grading_note: Formal parliamentary debate on Supply Bill 2026 proposing an explicit 2.5% wealth tax above a high threshold.

design_detail: wealth tax on multimillionaires and billionaires above US$1m
quote_original: maka adalah sepatutunya sampai pad awaktunya kerajaan mengenakan cukai kekayaan kepada orang-orang kaya ini, iaitu multimillionaire, maha jutawan, billionaire supaya jangan ada kekayaan ini berlegar di sekelliling beberapa kerat saja
quote_en: so it is duly time for the government to impose a wealth tax on these rich people, namely multimillionaires, tycoons, billionaires so that this wealth does not remain circulating among just a handful of people
source_title: Hassan Karim gesa kerajaan segera cukai ‘maha jutawan’
grading_note: Speech in Dewan Rakyat debate on Supply Bill 2026 proposing a wealth tax on multimillionaires and billionaires.

design_detail: wealth tax on multimillionaires and billionaires
quote_original: So in the same vein, I argue that it is time for the government to impose a wealth tax on the rich – the multimillionaires, the billionaires – so that wealth does not remain concentrated among just a handful of people.
source_title: Time for ultra-rich to pay wealth tax, says Hassan
grading_note: Public interview statement urging a wealth tax on the ultra-rich.

design_detail: 2%–2.5% on top 50 wealthiest people
quote_original: I am more attracted to the idea of a wealth tax... It would be like getting rid of a Lamborghini or something like that. It would not make much difference to them.
source_title: 'Like giving up a Lamborghini': Santiago says wealth tax on super-rich could raise RM10 bil
grading_note: Podcast statement proposing a 2% to 2.5% wealth tax on Malaysia's 50 richest people.

design_detail: 2% on net assets between RM1bn and RM2bn up to 10% on >RM30bn
quote_original: PSM mencadangkan satu cukai baru ke atas kekayaan individu dengan aset yang melebihi RM1 bilion... Golongan terkaya ini harus dicukai dengan kadar 2% untuk mereka yang memiliki aset bernilai antara RM1 bilion hingga ke RM2 bilion. Kadar cukai kekayaan harus ditingkatkan secara berperingkat ke 10% untuk mereka yang memiliki RM30 bilion ke atas.
quote_en: PSM proposes a new tax on individual wealth with assets exceeding RM1 billion... The richest group should be taxed at a rate of 2% for those with assets valued between RM1 billion and RM2 billion. The wealth tax rate should be graduated up to 10% for those with RM30 billion and above.
source_title: Kemelesetan ekonomi pasca COVID-19: Cadangan PSM untuk pulihkan negara demi rakyat
grading_note: Authored PSM policy document setting out a graduated wealth tax on billionaires from 2% to 10%.

design_detail: wealth tax on individuals with assets exceeding RM500m
quote_original: Imposing a wealth tax on individuals who have assets exceeding RM500m
source_title: How the government can increase its revenue over the long term
grading_note: Policy memorandum proposing a wealth tax on net assets exceeding RM500 million.

design_detail: wealth tax on Malaysia's 50 richest individuals
quote_original: Timbalan pengerusi PSM S Arutchelvan hari ini menggesa agar cukai kekayaan diperkenalkan berikutan laporan bahawa lima puluh orang terkaya di Malaysia meningkatkan kekayaan mereka.
quote_en: PSM deputy chairman S Arutchelvan today urged that a wealth tax be introduced following reports that the fifty richest people in Malaysia increased their wealth.
source_title: PSM gesa cukai kekayaan diperkenal
grading_note: Public statement urging a wealth tax on the 50 richest tycoons.

design_detail: party congress resolution calling for wealth tax
quote_original: Kerajaan harus melaksanakan sistem percukaian yang lebih progresif bagi mengurangkan ketidaksamaan dalam pengagihan kekayaan, dengan memperkenalkan cukai pusaka, cukai kekayaan dan cukai ke atas rumah kedua atau rumah yang dibiarkan kosong.
quote_en: The government should implement a more progressive tax system to reduce inequality in wealth distribution, by introducing inheritance tax, wealth tax and a tax on second homes or vacant houses.
source_title: Resolusi Kongres Nasional PSM ke-28
grading_note: Formal resolution adopted at the 28th National Congress of Parti Sosialis Malaysia.

design_detail: 2% wealth tax on top 50 richest individuals in Malaysia
quote_original: Cukai kekayaan sebanyak dua peratus akan membolehkan kerajaan mengutip RM8.3 bilion – iaitu 60 peratus lebih banyak daripada RM5 bilion yang disasarkan melalui kenaikan SST.
quote_en: A two percent wealth tax would enable the government to collect RM8.3 billion – 60 percent more than the RM5 billion targeted through the SST hike.
source_title: SST: Kenapa cukai pisang bukan maha kaya, soal NGO
grading_note: Campaign proposal advocating a 2% wealth tax on Malaysia's top 50 billionaires.

design_detail: 2% on 50 richest Malaysians
quote_original: Menurut laporan Unicef, keluarga berpendapatan rendah membelanjakan 38 peratus daripada pendapatan mereka untuk membeli makanan... Namun kita masih terus mengenakan cukai ke atas penggunaan, bukannya kekayaan
quote_en: According to the Unicef report, low-income families spend 38 percent of their income on food. Yet we still continue to impose taxes on consumption, rather than wealth
source_title: SST: Kenapa cukai pisang bukan maha kaya, soal NGO
grading_note: Public statement calling for a 2% wealth tax on top billionaires instead of taxing consumption. Review: regraded A to B: the quote contrasts taxing consumption with taxing wealth; the 2% figure is from the same press statement, not the quote.

design_detail: Option 1: 2% on top 100; Option 2: 1% >RM100m, 1.5% >RM500m
quote_original: Option 1: A 2% tax on the top 100 richest people in Malaysia... Option 2: A broader, graduated wealth tax – 1% on wealth above RM100m and 1.5% on wealth above RM500m.
source_title: Could a wealth tax fix Malaysia’s inequality crisis?
grading_note: Authored op-ed detailing specific rate and threshold designs for wealth taxation in Malaysia.

design_detail: 2% wealth tax on top wealth concentration
quote_original: The Ministry of Finance recently said in a statement that Malaysia has "no plans" to introduce a 2% wealth tax, because the country's tax base is "small and limited". But this raises a fundamental question. If the tax base is indeed narrow, why does the government continue to refuse to tax the greatest concentration of wealth in the country?
source_title: Progressive tax, regressive logic
grading_note: Op-ed critiquing the government for rejecting a 2% wealth tax.

design_detail: tax on wealth and excess profits
quote_original: He said governments should target tax on excess profits and wealth, raising the concern that rich corporations and individuals paid less and less in direct taxes, while the public paid more and more in indirect taxation, typically on consumption.
source_title: Commentary: GE15 - Fixing Malaysia’s healthcare system will require money, not just election pledges
grading_note: Argued that governments should target direct tax on excess profits and wealth rather than regressive consumption.

design_detail: high-exemption wealth tax targeting concentrated capital
quote_original: Merely increasing income tax or making income tax more progressive but without re-distributive means would not cure the issue of wealth disparity. The argument of wealth tax stifling economic growth and innovation is typically false as most innovation is produced by young, not wealthy individuals who would not be impacted by a high-exemption wealth tax
source_title: Tax! Tax! Tax! For the Common Good
grading_note: Policy analysis by think tank defending a high-exemption wealth tax.

design_detail: high-exemption wealth tax targeting top 1%
quote_original: Merely increasing income tax or making income tax more progressive but without re-distributive means would not cure the issue of wealth disparity. The argument of wealth tax stifling economic growth and innovation is typically false as most innovation is produced by young, not wealthy individuals who would not be impacted by a high-exemption wealth tax, where the wealthy often "own" and put in patents rather than innovate.
source_title: Tax! Tax! Tax! For the Common Good
grading_note: Interview on tax policy defending wealth taxation as essential to address wealth concentration.

design_detail: wealth tax on the wealthy class
quote_original: As usual, truly impactful measures like increasing corporate taxes and imposing wealth and inheritance taxes were glaringly absent from the budget... As things stand, the government's fiscal position remains strained precisely because it is stubbornly reluctant to impose such progressive taxes.
source_title: Budget 2027: Deliberately avoiding the big picture
grading_note: Commentary advocating the introduction of wealth taxation in the national budget.

design_detail: wealth tax on top 50 richest individuals
quote_original: Given the sheer amount of wealth these individuals possess and the current dire socioeconomic conditions many face, surely it would not be unreasonable for the government to impose a wealth tax on this particular group so that more funds are available to help support the majority?
source_title: LETTER | We need progressive taxation now
grading_note: Letter in Malaysiakini arguing for a wealth tax on the top 50 richest listees.

design_detail: wealth tax to fund public healthcare
quote_original: A form of wealth tax could be a source of funding that support and enhance public healthcare and other services. But finding the right balance of how to do so will always be tricky
source_title: Commentary: GE15 - Fixing Malaysia’s healthcare system will require money, not just election pledges
grading_note: Policy commentary advocating for a wealth tax to fund public health services.

design_detail: wealth tax on individuals with extraordinary wealth alongside inheritance and capital gains taxes
quote_original: Persoalan saya, kenapakah kerajaan tidak ada keberanian untuk mengenakan cukai-cukai yang baharu kepada golongan yang mempunyai kekayaan yang luar biasa? Seperti inheritance tax, wealth tax dan capital gains tax (CGT)... Kenapakah kerajaan tidak melakukan sistem pencukaian yang lebih adil yang mengenakan cukai kepada golongan yang mempunyai kekayaan yang luar biasa?
quote_en: My question is, why does the government not have the courage to impose new taxes on those who possess extraordinary wealth? Such as inheritance tax, wealth tax and capital gains tax (CGT)... Why does the government not implement a fairer taxation system that imposes taxes on those who have extraordinary wealth?
source_title: Penyata Rasmi Parlimen Dewan Rakyat DR 16.12.2020
grading_note: Hansard DR 16.12.2020 p. 32; explicit intervention in Dewan Rakyat proposing wealth tax on extraordinary wealth.

design_detail: 2.5% wealth tax on unutilised assets modelled on Islamic zakat harta and European wealth taxes
quote_original: Kalau kita melaksanakan cukai kemewahan, wealth tax di mana kita fikirkan ini sebenarnya bersesuaian dengan Islam di mana zakat harta. Setiap tahun kita kena buatkan kira-kira kita, berapa aset kita yang tersimpan dan tidak digunakan dan membayar 2.5%. Ini maknanya konsep sudah ada dalam Islam, zakat harta itu digunakan dalam negara barat seperti Norway seperti Netherlands dan apa salahnya kita juga memikirkan pada tahun 2016, inilah cara-caranya untuk kita menambahkan hasil kerajaan.
quote_en: If we implement a luxury tax, wealth tax where we consider that this is actually consistent with Islam in terms of property zakat. Every year we have to do our calculation, how much of our assets are stored and not used and pay 2.5%. This means the concept already exists in Islam, property zakat is used in Western countries like Norway like the Netherlands, and what is wrong with us also considering for 2016, these are the ways for us to increase government revenue.
source_title: Penyata Rasmi Parlimen Dewan Rakyat DR 16.10.2014
grading_note: Hansard DR 16.10.2014 p. 30; speech in Dewan Rakyat budget debate proposing a 2.5% annual wealth tax on stored assets.

design_detail: Global millionaire tax / wealth tax on ultra-rich individuals generating RM1bn annually
quote_original: Sudah tiba masanya kita meletakkan tumpuan kepada golongan jutawan di negara kita yang sebenarnya lebih wajar untuk menyumbang lebih kepada pendapatan negara. Saya ingin mencadangkan kepada kerajaan untuk melaksanakan cukai jutawan global di Malaysia. Sebenarnya jurang kekayaan yang semakin melebar di negara kita membangkitkan gesaan supaya rakyat terkaya menanggung lebih banyak beban cukai... kerajaan Malaysia wajar membuka bidang baharu bagi membanteras amalan mengelak cukai dengan mengenakan cukai minimum global ke atas golongan jutawan. Ia dijangka boleh menjana pendapatan negara sebanyak RM1 bilion pada setiap tahun.
quote_en: It is high time we place our focus on the millionaires in our country who are genuinely more appropriate to contribute more to national revenue. I wish to propose to the government to implement a global millionaire tax in Malaysia. In reality the widening wealth gap in our country raises calls for the richest citizens to bear more of the tax burden... the Government of Malaysia should open new frontiers to combat tax avoidance by imposing a global minimum tax on millionaires. It is expected to be able to generate RM1 billion in national revenue every year.
source_title: Penyata Rasmi Parlimen Dewan Negara DN 30.11.2023
grading_note: Hansard DN 30.11.2023 pp. 34-35; speech in Dewan Negara debating the 2024 Supply Bill.

design_detail: 2% annual wealth tax on net accumulated assets of billionaires (stocks, real estate, private business holdings)
quote_original: Kita boleh mengenakan cukai kekayaan aset ke atas bilionair-bilionair di Malaysia... Tidak seperti cukai pendapatan tradisional, yang menyasarkan pendapatan tahunan, cukai Zucman menyasarkan stok kekayaan terkumpul – aset seperti saham, hartanah dan pegangan pemilikan dalam syarikat swasta... Para bilionair negara harus menyumbang balik kepada negara dan rela membayar cukai kekayaan aset ini supaya negara lebih makmur dan ada lebih banyak dana untuk menyediakan perkhidmatan awam yang murah dan berkualiti tinggi yang boleh dinikmati bersama.
quote_en: We can impose an asset wealth tax on billionaires in Malaysia... Unlike traditional income tax, which targets annual income, the Zucman tax targets the accumulated stock of wealth – assets like shares, real estate and ownership holdings in private companies... The country's billionaires must contribute back to the country and willingly pay this asset wealth tax so that the nation is more prosperous and has more funds to provide affordable, high quality public services that can be enjoyed together.
source_title: Selesaikan masalah kesesakan hospital: Cukai ke atas kekayaan aset bilionair
grading_note: Op-ed for PSM health initiative proposing an annual 2% wealth tax on billionaire asset stocks to fund public hospital infrastructure.

design_detail: wealth tax on ultra-rich individuals with assets exceeding RM500 million
quote_original: Di samping usaha serantau ini, Malaysia juga perlu melaksanakan pembaharuan percukaian secara dalaman, termasuk: Memperkenalkan cukai kekayaan terhadap individu ultra-kaya yang memiliki aset melebihi RM500 juta.
quote_en: Alongside these regional efforts, Malaysia must also implement domestic taxation reforms, including: Introducing a wealth tax on ultra-rich individuals who own assets exceeding RM500 million.
source_title: Mengapa Malaysia Tidak Bangkitkan Isu Cukai Korporat di Peringkat ASEAN?
grading_note: Official statement by PSM Central Committee Member calling for domestic wealth tax on individuals owning > RM500m in assets.

design_detail: 2-3% annual wealth tax on net worth of richest individuals
quote_original: Anil Netto says it is about time the government considers imposing a wealth tax aimed at the ultra-wealthy... His ideas have been taken up in the US by presidential candidate Senator Elizabeth Warren, who together with economists, has crafted a proposed 2-3% annual wealth tax on the net worth of the richest... So instead of narrowing the debate to whether SST or GST is a better consumption tax, isn't it about time we consider wealth taxes?
quote_en: Anil Netto says it is about time the government considers imposing a wealth tax aimed at the ultra-wealthy... His ideas have been taken up in the US by presidential candidate Senator Elizabeth Warren, who together with economists, has crafted a proposed 2-3% annual wealth tax on the net worth of the richest... So instead of narrowing the debate to whether SST or GST is a better consumption tax, isn't it about time we consider wealth taxes?
source_title: SST vs GST: A false debate
grading_note: Opinion analysis published on Aliran calling for a 2-3% annual net wealth tax on the richest individuals.

design_detail: raising wealth taxes alongside death duties to finance social spending for B40 and M40
quote_original: Ramon said through the 2019 Budget, the rich could do much more to help the B40 and the M40 income groups, such as by raising the wealth tax, death duty and inheritance tax.
quote_en: Ramon said through the 2019 Budget, the rich could do much more to help the B40 and the M40 income groups, such as by raising the wealth tax, death duty and inheritance tax.
source_title: Gov't not neglecting M40 income group, says Asli chair
grading_note: Interview with Malaysiakini following the 2019 budget advocating for raising wealth taxes to assist the B40 and M40.

design_detail: progressive 0.5%-1.75% (or 1.0%-3.5%) wealth tax on net assets exceeding RM10m, modelled on Spanish Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio
quote_original: Berdasarkan bilangan individu amat kaya... yang direkodkan oleh Buku Data Kekayaan Global 2018 yang diterbitkan oleh Credit Suisse serta cadangan pengenaan kadar cukai progresif 0.5%-1.75% terhadap individu yang bernilai lebih daripada RM10 juta, anggaran jumlah kutipan cukai adalah RM13.186 bilion... Premis ini bertindak sebagai asas keperluan cukai kekayaan. Malaysia boleh mengikut jejak langkah Negara Sepanyol yang mengenakan cukai kekayaan terhadap semua aset bersih... Secara konklusi, cukai kekayaan patut diperkenalkan untuk mengatasi masalah kesenjangan kekayaan, meningkatkan hasil kerajaan serta membantu negara Malaysia membayar balik hutang negara yang tinggi.
quote_en: Based on the number of ultra-wealthy individuals... recorded by the Global Wealth Databook 2018 published by Credit Suisse and the proposed imposition of progressive tax rates of 0.5%-1.75% on individuals worth more than RM10 million, the estimated total tax revenue is RM13.186 billion... This premise acts as the basis for the necessity of a wealth tax. Malaysia can follow in the footsteps of Spain, which imposes a wealth tax on all net assets... In conclusion, a wealth tax should be introduced to overcome wealth inequality, increase government revenue and help Malaysia pay back its high national debt.
source_title: Saranan Cukai Kekayaan
grading_note: Comprehensive think tank policy proposal modeling progressive wealth taxation on net assets exceeding RM10m based on Spanish design.

design_detail: 2% wealth tax on ultra-high-net-worth individuals based on Gabriel Zucman report
quote_original: The response to my proposal for a 2% wealth tax is welcome. The G20 endorsed the 2% figure in 2024 following economist Gabriel Zucman's report, which proposed it as the minimum floor for effectively taxing ultra-high-net-worth individuals... But income tax and wealth tax are not the same. Income tax applies to what a person earns in a year, while a wealth tax applies to accumulated assets that often grow far faster than any worker's wages ever will... A 2% wealth tax is not radical. If Malaysia can ask ordinary families to bear higher costs through consumption taxes and subsidy cuts, then it can also ask its wealthiest citizens to return a small fraction of the wealth this country has helped make possible.
quote_en: The response to my proposal for a 2% wealth tax is welcome. The G20 endorsed the 2% figure in 2024 following economist Gabriel Zucman's report, which proposed it as the minimum floor for effectively taxing ultra-high-net-worth individuals... But income tax and wealth tax are not the same. Income tax applies to what a person earns in a year, while a wealth tax applies to accumulated assets that often grow far faster than any worker's wages ever will... A 2% wealth tax is not radical. If Malaysia can ask ordinary families to bear higher costs through consumption taxes and subsidy cuts, then it can also ask its wealthiest citizens to return a small fraction of the wealth this country has helped make possible.
source_title: There is justification for 2% wealth tax proposal
grading_note: Op-ed explaining justification for a 2% annual wealth tax on accumulated assets of the ultra-rich.

design_detail: progressive wealth tax (2% to 10%) on held assets exceeding RM1 billion
quote_original: Wealth tax is a tax levied on the value of held assets where tax will be applicable to a variety of asset types including cash, bank deposits, shares, fixed assets, personal cars, assessed value of real property, pension plans, money funds, owner-occupied housing, and trusts. We propose this tax only on those that have a declared wealth of RM1 billion and above. It would be a progressive tax starting from 2% up top 10%... Thus if the government taxes the 50 wealthiest Malaysians progressively it will generate approximately RM 20 billion per year from the billionaires.
quote_en: Wealth tax is a tax levied on the value of held assets where tax will be applicable to a variety of asset types including cash, bank deposits, shares, fixed assets, personal cars, assessed value of real property, pension plans, money funds, owner-occupied housing, and trusts. We propose this tax only on those that have a declared wealth of RM1 billion and above. It would be a progressive tax starting from 2% up top 10%... Thus if the government taxes the 50 wealthiest Malaysians progressively it will generate approximately RM 20 billion per year from the billionaires.
source_title: Despicable to even think of GST !
grading_note: Official policy statement by PSM Secretary-General proposing progressive net wealth tax on billionaires.

design_detail: 10% emergency wealth tax on the 50 richest Malaysians to fund targeted basic income
quote_original: Kerajaan sewajarnya mengenakan “cukai kecemasan” sebanyak 10% terhadap 50 orang terkaya di Malaysia yang akan menjana hampir RM37 bilion untuk melaksanakan skim Pendapatan Asas Bersasar. Pada tahun 2020, ekonomi negara telah merosot sebanyak 5.6% tetapi kekayaan 50 orang terkaya di negara telah meningkat sebanyak 14% kepada RM374 bilion (US$90billion).
quote_en: The government should impose an "emergency tax" of 10% on the 50 richest people in Malaysia which would generate nearly RM37 billion to implement a Targeted Basic Income scheme. In 2020, the country's economy contracted by 5.6% but the wealth of the 50 richest people in the country increased by 14% to RM374 billion (US$90 billion).
source_title: Menteri Kewangan gagal faham impak pengeluaran KWSP sebelum bersara
grading_note: Article by PSM Central Committee member proposing a 10% emergency wealth levy on the 50 richest Malaysians.

design_detail: progressive wealth tax on the top 0.01% of wealth holders
quote_original: A tax on fewer than 0.01% of people in Malaysia... through a wealth tax... could raise an extra RM10bn a year. This money that would go a long way towards the country’s social and economic development.
quote_en: A tax on fewer than 0.01% of people in Malaysia... through a wealth tax... could raise an extra RM10bn a year. This money that would go a long way towards the country’s social and economic development.
source_title: Beyond GST vs SST: A fairer way to tax
grading_note: Op-ed on Aliran by development economist advocating progressive taxation on top 0.01% including wealth tax.

design_detail: broader wealth or capital gains taxes on top percentiles of wealth owners
quote_original: Laying the groundwork for tax reforms requires intensified and broader structural efforts. While initiatives, such as mandated e-invoicing, the rollout of a taxpayer identification number (TIN) and enhanced tax compliance enforcement are important steps towards modernising the tax system, these efforts must be expanded to build the necessary infrastructure for future wealth and capital gains taxation. This includes developing robust valuation mechanisms for assets and improving data collection on capital income. In the longer term, more comprehensive reforms – such as broader wealth or capital gains taxes – will be essential to share the tax burden with the top percentiles of wealth owners and ensure long-term revenue sustainability in line with the stated intention of Budget 2025. Without deeper and bolder reforms, current measures might risk being more symbolic than substantive in addressing wealth inequality and progressing on the equitable taxation of wealth.
quote_en: Laying the groundwork for tax reforms requires intensified and broader structural efforts. While initiatives, such as mandated e-invoicing, the rollout of a taxpayer identification number (TIN) and enhanced tax compliance enforcement are important steps towards modernising the tax system, these efforts must be expanded to build the necessary infrastructure for future wealth and capital gains taxation. This includes developing robust valuation mechanisms for assets and improving data collection on capital income. In the longer term, more comprehensive reforms – such as broader wealth or capital gains taxes – will be essential to share the tax burden with the top percentiles of wealth owners and ensure long-term revenue sustainability in line with the stated intention of Budget 2025. Without deeper and bolder reforms, current measures might risk being more symbolic than substantive in addressing wealth inequality and progressing on the equitable taxation of wealth.
source_title: Policy insights into Budget 2025: fiscal reforms, social protection, energy and climate action
archive_url: Institute of Strategic & International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia
grading_note: Policy research note (p. 12) advocating infrastructure preparation for wealth taxation and broader wealth taxes. Review: regraded A to B: advocates preparing for and later broader wealth or capital gains taxes, no design.

design_detail: broader wealth or capital gains taxes on top percentiles of wealth owners
quote_original: In the longer term, more comprehensive reforms – such as broader wealth or capital gains taxes – will be essential to share the tax burden with the top percentiles of wealth owners and ensure long-term revenue sustainability in line with the stated intention of Budget 2025. Without deeper and bolder reforms, current measures might risk being more symbolic than substantive in addressing wealth inequality and progressing on the equitable taxation of wealth.

Without deeper and bolder reforms, current measures might risk being more symbolic than substantive in addressing wealth inequality and progressing on the equitable taxation of wealth.
source_title: Policy insights into Budget 2025: fiscal reforms, social protection, energy and climate action
archive_url: Institute of Strategic & International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia
grading_note: Co-author and Fellow of Economics Trade and Regional Integration at ISIS Malaysia; policy research note p. 12. Review: regraded A to B: names broader wealth or capital gains taxes as a longer-term reform, no design.

design_detail: 2.5% wealth tax on shares (RM1.9tn) and corporate savings (RM500bn) modelled on Islamic zakat and European wealth taxes
quote_original: Cukai kekayaan yang hari ini kalau kita lihat di England sebagai contoh, sedang bincang cukai kekayaan dua persen dan kita lihat dalam Islam mencadangkan untuk kita mengambil cukai terhadap kekayaan mereka yang melabur dalam saham dan cukai terhadap simpanan korporat... Bila masanya, sedangkan kalau kita lihat dalam Islam sendiri, cukai berasaskan saham adalah cukai yang dikenakan kepada mereka yang terlibat dengan saham, 2.5 persen. Kalau kita lihat angka yang saya sebut sebelum ini, nilai pegangan saham pada tahun 2018 sebanyak RM1.9 trilion, kalau dikenakan cukai sebanyak 2.5 persen, kita mendapat RM47.5 bilion... Samalah juga dengan simpanan korporat. Simpanan korporat kita buat unjuran sekitar RM500 bilion. Jika dikenakan cukai terhadap simpanan korporat, dengan 2.5 persen kita boleh mendapat hasil sekitar RM12 bilion. Saya ingin menyatakan bahawa, sampai masa kerajaan untuk melihat kembali kaedah percukaian negara dibuat reformasi dan melihat kaedah Islam yang lebih baik, lebih adil dan memberi hak kepada rakyat.
quote_en: Wealth tax which today if we look at England for example, is discussing a two percent wealth tax, and we see in Islam proposing for us to take tax on the wealth of those who invest in shares and tax on corporate savings... When is the time, whereas if we look at Islam itself, tax based on shares is a tax imposed on those involved with shares, 2.5 percent. If we look at the figures I mentioned earlier, the value of shareholdings in 2018 was RM1.9 trillion, if a tax of 2.5 percent is imposed, we get RM47.5 billion... Likewise with corporate savings. Corporate savings we project around RM500 billion. If taxed against corporate savings, at 2.5 percent we can obtain revenue around RM12 billion. I wish to state that, the time has arrived for the government to revisit the country's taxation methods with reform and look at the Islamic method which is better, fairer and gives rights to the people.
source_title: Penyata Rasmi Parlimen Dewan Rakyat DR 16.10.2019
grading_note: Hansard DR 16.10.2019 pp. 98-99; speech in Dewan Rakyat 2020 budget debate proposing 2.5% wealth tax on shares and corporate savings.

design_detail: 2% wealth tax on ultra-wealthy individuals to prevent cuts to public healthcare budget
quote_original: TUAN HASSAN BIN ABDUL KARIM [PASIR GUDANG] minta MENTERI KEWANGAN menyatakan adakah Kerajaan bersetuju kaedah penyelesaian supaya belanjawan Kementerian Kesihatan tidak dipotong ialah dengan Kerajaan memperkenalkan Cukai Kekayaan (Wealth Tax) sebanyak dua peratus levi ke atas individu kaya-raya.
quote_en: MR HASSAN BIN ABDUL KARIM [PASIR GUDANG] asks the MINISTER OF FINANCE to state whether the Government agrees that the solution to prevent the Ministry of Health budget from being cut is for the Government to introduce a Wealth Tax of two percent levy on ultra-wealthy individuals.
source_title: Penyata Rasmi Parlimen Dewan Rakyat JDR 15.07.2026
grading_note: Hansard JDR 15.07.2026 p. 241 Question No. 83; formal oral question submitted to Dewan Rakyat urging introduction of 2% wealth tax on the rich.
